raw_response:
I am sorry to hear that you are facing this stressful situation with your security deposit.

### | Your Situation
You vacated your rented premises, but your landlord is withholding the return of your security deposit without valid justification. This dispute involves the non-refund of deposited funds following the termination of your tenancy.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Guidelines & State Enactments) Section 11 & Section 13, the security deposit for residential premises is typically capped at a maximum of two months' rent, and landlords are required to refund it upon taking over vacant possession after making only valid, agreed-upon deductions.
- Under The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 108(m) & (o), you are only bound to restore the property subject to "reasonable wear and tear"—meaning landlords cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage or routine painting without an explicit contractual basis.
- Please note that legal outcomes depend heavily on specific document terms and evidence, and a successful court result can never be 100% guaranteed.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your written tenancy agreement, rent payment receipts, the handing-over possession receipt, and photographs or videos of the property's condition at the time of vacating.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your landlord clearly stating the amount due and granting a strict 15-day window for complete repayment of your security deposit.
3. If the landlord fails to respond or pay within 15 days, approach the appropriate local Rent Authority or consumer/civil forum having jurisdiction over the property.

### Information I still need from you
1. What is the exact amount of the security deposit your landlord is withholding, and how many months of rent did it represent?
2. Do you have a written and signed tenancy agreement, and did you sign a formal handing-over or move-out inspection document when you left?

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
